annotations.text:
Three directions for the portfolio overhaul — pick one and I'll build it out properly (desktop + mobile + working filters).

All three show the same two things so they're comparable: the hero with the one-year positioning, and four work entries.

Everything in [BRACKETS] is a real fact I don't have yet — your company, your work projects, the project count. The two university projects are real.

A — MISSION CONTROL

Why: keeps the space identity you already have, but disciplines it. Near-black instead of pure black, a faint technical grid instead of animated rockets, monospace data labels, a telemetry strip. Familiar, but it stops looking like a student site.

Tradeoff: it's still a themed site. Some recruiters read "space" as a gimmick no matter how well it's done.

B — EDITORIAL

Why: warm paper, serif headlines, projects as big numbered entries with room to actually explain them. Reads calm and senior — this is what a portfolio looks like when the work speaks for itself.

Tradeoff: throws the current identity away completely. A light theme is the biggest possible break from the site you have now.

C — TERMINAL

Why: monospace-first, IDE chrome, work as a sortable file listing. Dense and confident — signals "I write code" before you read a single word.

Tradeoff: speaks fluently to engineers, less so to HR screeners and non-technical recruiters, who are often the first people to open your link.
